output:
I checked the diff against every rule in the conventions checklist. It's docs-only: one commit (`343526055`) changing three files in `docs/agents/`, 6 lines added and 1 removed. I found one clear error and two smaller issues.

**How I ran it**
- I wrote the generated checklist to the scratchpad instead of `docs/engineering/`. The file isn't in `.gitignore` in this repo, so generating it there would have left an untracked file in the worktree. No tracked files changed.
- I didn't need to look up any rule's source learnings.

**Rules that applied:** CHANGE-01, CHANGE-02, CHANGE-04, PR-01, PR-02 and MOD-01. The other rules (types, DB, cache, auth, tests, logging, security and so on) don't apply to a docs-only diff.

**Passing checks**
- The change is small and scoped (CHANGE-01, CHANGE-02).
- All three files have their SPDX headers, and `git diff --check` is clean.
- The `cgw-*` skills only point to the `docs/agents/*` files, so the skill copies can't drift out of sync with these edits.
- The in-place removal exception in `api-dtos-and-validation.md` fits CHANGE-04, because it only covers contracts that were never released.
- The claim that `EntitlementsModule` is reached only through `BillingModule` is correct: `src/modules/billing/billing.module.ts` is its only importer, and `src/app.module.ts:97` doesn't register it directly.
- The "portfolio anti-example below" reference at `module-structure.md:33` points to a real paragraph (`module-structure.md:39`).

## Findings

**1. Medium (PR-02, docs match the code): `docs/agents/module-structure.md:133`**
The rule says a module can skip `app.module.ts` "when the new module only serves that one" module, and gives `backbone`, `email`, `siwe` and `queues` as examples "wired the same way". Two of those examples don't fit:
- **`siwe` serves two modules.** `SiweModule` is imported by both `AuthModule` (`src/modules/auth/auth.module.ts:10`) and `UsersModule` (`src/modules/users/users.module.ts:26`).
- **`email` and `queues` have no module file at their root.**
  - `email` is two separate submodules: `SesEmailModule` is used by `spaces`, and `EmailModule` (under `pushwoosh/`) is used by `alerts`.
  - `queues` has only a datasource module, `QueuesApiModule`, imported by `HealthModule`.

  So neither one shows "a module reached through its single parent". `email` is also listed as a structurally deviant module by the `cgw-module-structure` skill, which makes it an odd precedent to point to.

A reader could use `siwe` to justify an unregistered module that several others share. Fix: keep `backbone` as the example (only `ChainsModule` imports it), and either drop `siwe`, `email` and `queues` or reword the rule to "imported by already-registered modules".

**2. Low (PR-02 / the new exception's wording): `docs/agents/api-dtos-and-validation.md:113`**
"An endpoint that has sat behind a disabled feature flag since it was introduced" doesn't say which environment the flag was off in. Flags are set per environment (`configFactory().features`). If a flag is off in production but on in staging or dev, clients built against staging may already parse the field, and the exception would allow an in-place break for them. Fix: say "disabled in every deployed environment", or ask the PR description to state where the flag was off.

**3. Low (the "no stale guides" item in `reviewing.md` applies here): `docs/agents/reviewing.md:48`, `docs/agents/module-structure.md:33`**
The new staged-delivery exception (a `routes/` folder or other artifact that ships before the PR that uses it) is only added to `docs/agents/*`. The parallel conventions file, `docs/engineering/sources/rules.json`, isn't updated: PR-01 ("Can I justify every new abstraction or file?") and MOD-01 still say nothing about staged delivery. A reviewer running `/code-conventions --review-pr` on a follow-up PR in a declared series could flag exactly what this PR now allows. Fix: tighten PR-01's rule text to add the same "declared series + linked follow-up" condition, then regenerate `rules.generated.md`. Or say in the PR description that `rules.json` is intentionally left as is.

**Open questions:** none beyond the three findings.
